notes:
Lead source: doc-search tutorial / blog post -> self-serve signup.

Business context: small legal-tech startup building a searchable knowledge base for contracts and client memos. Want fast retrieval + accurate reranking for short legal Q&A and clause lookup.

Technical constraints / asks:
- Primary stack: Node.js service, Pinecone (v1) for vector store, PostgreSQL for metadata.
- Target latency: tail under 300ms for single-query rerank (100ms preferred for short queries).
- Throughput: modest (10-200 qps peak), mostly synchronous API calls from web UI.
- Cost profile: high sensitivity; prefer hosted API with predictable per-embedding + per-token pricing.
- Model preferences: open/quantized models (Llama2-13B quantized or Mistral variants) to control cost; OK with Redwood-verified model suggestions.
- Rerank flow questions: whether Redwood returns embeddings that are stable across model versions, recommended similarity + learned reranker pattern, and whether we can do hybrid search (bm25 + embeddings) with example code.
- Integration asks: batching best practices for bulk upsert to Pinecone, recommended embedding dimension, streaming vs non-streaming for retrieval+generation flows.

Quotes from CTO: "We need an end-to-end example — from ingest -> embeddings -> pinecone upsert -> retrieval + rerank + generation. If embeddings improve answer precision by 10% and cost stays lower than current, we'll move to paid."

Red flags / notes for AE: want quickstarter repo, clear SSO plan (SAML later), SOC2 evidence. Price sensitivity means start small; likely to convert if POC results are strong.
